title: ICU patient data collection for the ICUdata4EU project
summary:
The EU-funded ICUdata4EU project aims to improve the care of patients in intensive care units (ICUs) by making it easier and safer for hospitals across Europe to use clinical data for research. To achieve this, the project is building a shared technical infrastructure that allows hospitals to work together while keeping patient data securely under their own control. In the future, this infrastructure may also support AI-based research.

The project focuses on organizing routine clinical data into a common format so that it can be understood and used consistently across different hospitals and countries. The data is used only for scientific research and is not used for patient treatment.

Each project partner sets up two main components:

* A secure local system called the "Dataminer", which collects data from the hospital, checks its quality, removes identifying information, and converts it into a standardized format, 
* as well as a connection to a central hub, the "Data Marketplace", which allows researchers to discover what types of data are available across participating hospitals without accessing the data itself.

At UKA, an additional internal AI platform is required because of the large amount of data generated during everyday hospital operations. This platform simply gathers data from different hospital systems and prepares it in a common format before passing it to the Dataminer. It is connected only to internal hospital systems and the Dataminer and has no connection to the internet or other external networks.

After the Dataminer has processed the data, it stores it securely in a local database within the hospital.

Researchers from other project partners can submit requests for data through the Data Marketplace for specific scientific studies. The Marketplace first checks whether participating hospitals have relevant datasets by comparing only metadata (information about the data, not the data itself). If a hospital has suitable data, it can choose to provide controlled access through its Dataminer. The actual data always remains at the hospital where it was collected and never leaves its secure environment, ensuring that each hospital retains full control over its data.

Overall, the project is creating a Europe-wide network of intensive care data rather than a single central database. Patient data is standardized, double-pseudonymized, and stored locally by each participating hospital. Researchers can analyze relevant data for approved scientific projects without the data being transferred out of the hospital.

By enabling researchers and clinicians across Europe to learn from a much larger pool of intensive care data, the project is expected to improve medical research, support collaboration between hospitals, and ultimately lead to better care for intensive care patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Must have signed a declaration of consent.
Must be patients from the OIM and Weaning stations: OIM 1, OI2A 01-07, OIM2 08-21, OIM 3, OIM 4, OIM 6/7, WEA
Must have a treatment outcome (deceased or discharged)
Exclusion criteria:
Younger than 18 y.o.
No declaration of consent signed
Not a patient of the OIM or Weaning stations
Patient still in the station
